grounding.states: For large eggs dropped into boiling water, 12 minutes gives fully hard-boiled eggs
grounding.from: Healthline says 12 to 13 minutes gives fully hard-boiled eggs that are not over-cooked

grounding.states: 10 minutes gives a firm yolk that may be slightly soft in the center
grounding.from: At 10 minutes, the eggs are mostly cooked through but slightly soft in the center

grounding.states: Past about 14 to 15 minutes the eggs turn rubbery or dry
grounding.from: 15 minutes gives rubbery whites and powdery dry yolks; Past about 14–15 minutes the eggs turn rubbery or dry

grounding.states: Smaller eggs cook quicker and larger ones need extra time
grounding.from: smaller ones cook quicker while larger ones need extra time

value.answer: For large eggs dropped into boiling water, go 12 minutes for a fully set yolk. 10 is firm but can still be a bit soft in the middle, and past about 14 minutes they get rubbery and dry. Smaller eggs cook a little quicker, bigger ones need a bit longer.
